tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-verification.md <<'EOF'
# TLS certificate verification

The project's current recorded decision is that TLS certificate verification stays enabled on all builds, development builds included, and no build type is exempt. This is consistent with the recorded rule that HTTPS is used everywhere, with no plaintext exceptions.
EOF
cat docs/policies/tls-verification.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-verification.md` with a one-paragraph statement. It says TLS certificate verification stays on for all builds, development builds included, with no exemptions.

It rests on the recorded decision #26, "verification on all builds", which withdrew an earlier decision, #24. I left the withdrawn decision out of the file. The paragraph also notes that this fits decision #29, "HTTPS everywhere, no plaintext exceptions", which is also current.

My first attempt to write the file through the shell failed with a parser error, so I used the Write tool instead. The file is written, but I didn't read it back.
